switch.title: Dead Man's Switch Email for Encrypted Files | AnyCircumstances
switch.description: Set recurring check-ins, email reminders, a grace period, and trusted recipients. If you stop responding, AnyCircumstances can securely release assigned files.
switch.h1: A Dead Man's Switch for Email, Check-Ins, and Encrypted Files
switch.intro: A digital dead man's switch waits for a signal from you. With AnyCircumstances, that signal is a scheduled check-in. If you miss one, your grace period begins. If you still do not respond before the grace period expires, your designated recipients are emailed secure access to the files you assigned to them.

sections.heading: How a dead man's switch email works
paragraphs: When people search for a dead man's switch email, they are usually looking for a system that contacts someone automatically if they stop responding. The safest version is not a single delayed email waiting to fire. It uses repeated check-ins, reminders, and a grace period so one forgotten deadline does not immediately release sensitive information.
AnyCircumstances uses that model. You choose the check-in schedule, choose how reminders are sent, set the grace period, and decide which recipients should receive which files.

cards.heading: A check-in becomes due
cards.text: AnyCircumstances expects a scheduled confirmation from you.

cards.heading: You receive email reminders
cards.text: Reminder emails are sent according to the reminder settings you configured.

cards.heading: You check in
cards.text: Enter your PIN to confirm the check-in.

cards.heading: You miss the check-in
cards.text: Missing the deadline does not immediately notify recipients. Your configured grace period begins.

cards.heading: You still have time to respond
cards.text: You can check in during the grace period and stop the pending release.

cards.heading: The grace period expires
cards.text: If you still have not checked in, the release process begins.

cards.heading: Recipients are emailed
cards.text: Each designated recipient receives a secure link for accessing the files assigned to them.

sections.heading: A missed check-in is not proof of death
paragraphs: AnyCircumstances does not determine whether you are alive, dead, injured, traveling, offline, or simply unavailable. It responds to the check-in rules you configured. That is why reminders and a grace period matter: they create time to recover from a missed deadline before recipient delivery occurs.

cards.heading: Cryptocurrency recovery context
cards.text: A dead man's switch can deliver encrypted instructions about where cryptocurrency is held, which devices matter, which exchange accounts exist, and what recovery steps a trusted person may need. It does not transfer legal ownership of cryptocurrency and should not be treated as a substitute for estate planning.

vault.title: Secure Digital Vault for Important Documents | AnyCircumstances
vault.description: A personal digital vault for encrypted documents, emergency information, recovery instructions, and controlled delivery to trusted recipients.
vault.h1: A Secure Digital Vault for Important Documents and Emergency Information
vault.intro: Store important documents and instructions in an encrypted vault instead of leaving them in an ordinary shared folder. AnyCircumstances adds recurring check-ins and controlled recipient delivery so the files can stay private until your release conditions are met.

sections.heading: What can a personal digital vault hold?
paragraphs: A personal digital vault is useful for information that is private today but may become important to somebody else later.

cards.heading: Important documents
cards.text: Insurance policies, property records, contracts, identification copies, estate documents, and directions to authoritative originals.

cards.heading: Account instructions
cards.text: A map of important accounts, password-manager instructions, recovery contacts, backup-code locations, and notes explaining what someone should handle first.

cards.heading: Emergency information
cards.text: Medical contacts, insurance details, household instructions, pet or dependent-care information, and other details someone may need quickly.

cards.heading: Cryptocurrency instructions
cards.text: Notes about Bitcoin, Ethereum, hardware wallets, exchange accounts, devices, wallet locations, and recovery procedures. Avoid placing raw secrets in ordinary unencrypted notes.

cards.heading: Personal directions
cards.text: Letters, explanations, business-continuity instructions, contact lists, or context that would otherwise exist only in your head.

sections.heading: Is a digital vault the same as electronic vaulting?
paragraphs: The terms overlap. "Digital vault," "electronic vault," and "electronic vaulting" are often used for protected electronic storage. What matters is the security and access model behind the name. A useful vault should explain how files are encrypted, who can access them, how recovery works, and what happens when the owner is unavailable.

sections.heading: Online vault for documents vs ordinary cloud storage
paragraphs: A normal cloud drive is designed for everyday syncing, sharing, and collaboration. A secure document vault is better suited to files that should remain private and deliberately controlled. AnyCircumstances adds a second layer to the storage problem: it lets you decide who should receive selected encrypted files if your check-in and grace-period conditions are eventually met.

links.label: Compare digital vaults and cloud storage

cards.heading: A vault with a release plan
cards.text: AnyCircumstances combines encrypted storage with configurable check-ins, reminders, a grace period, and trusted-recipient delivery. It is designed to make emergency access deliberate instead of giving someone permanent access in advance.

how.title: How AnyCircumstances Check-Ins & Emergency Delivery Work
how.description: See the full flow: encrypted files, trusted recipients, scheduled check-ins, email reminders, a customizable grace period, and secure recipient delivery.
how.eyebrow: FROM PRIVATE STORAGE TO CONTROLLED DELIVERY
how.intro: Store important files in an encrypted vault, choose the people who may eventually need them, and create a check-in schedule. As long as you keep checking in, your files stay private. If you stop responding and your grace period expires, your designated recipients are emailed secure access to the files you assigned to them.

sections.heading: The full check-in and release flow

cards.heading: Encrypt and upload your files
cards.text: Choose the files you want to protect. They are encrypted on your device before upload, so the storage service receives encrypted data instead of the original readable file.

cards.heading: Choose trusted recipients
cards.text: Add the people who should receive specific files if your release conditions are eventually met. Different files can be assigned according to who actually needs them.

cards.heading: Choose your check-in schedule
cards.text: Set how often AnyCircumstances should expect you to check in. A successful check-in confirms that you still have access to your account and resets the schedule.

cards.heading: Configure your email reminders
cards.text: Reminder emails are sent according to the reminder settings you configured.

cards.heading: Set your grace period
cards.text: Choose how much extra time you want after a missed check-in. The grace period exists so one forgotten deadline does not immediately release sensitive files.

cards.heading: You check in
cards.text: Enter your PIN to confirm the check-in.

cards.heading: If you miss a check-in, the grace period begins
cards.text: Nothing is released immediately. You can still complete a successful check-in during the grace period and stop the pending release.

cards.heading: If the grace period expires, recipient delivery begins
cards.text: If you still have not checked in when the grace period ends, the designated recipients are emailed a secure link for accessing the files assigned to them.

sections.heading: What happens if I miss a check-in?
paragraphs: Missing a check-in is recoverable. The system is designed to give you another window to respond before recipient delivery occurs.

sections.heading: What does a recipient receive?
paragraphs: The recipient receives an email containing a secure link for accessing the files assigned to them. The recipient does not automatically receive every file in your account. Access follows the recipient and file assignments you configured.

sections.heading: A check-in is a trigger, not a determination
paragraphs: AnyCircumstances does not decide whether you have died or whether an emergency has occurred. It only knows whether the check-in conditions you configured were completed. The system follows those rules exactly, which is why choosing a realistic schedule, reliable reminders, and a sensible grace period matters.

branch.missed: Your scheduled check-in passes without confirmation.
branch.grace: Your configured grace period begins and reminders continue according to your settings.

left.heading: You check in
left.text: The pending release stops, the schedule resets, and your recipients are not contacted.

right.heading: You do not check in
right.text: When the grace period expires, the release process begins and designated recipients are emailed.

sections.heading: What should be in an emergency information vault?
paragraphs: Start with the information another person would need to understand your situation without having you there to explain it.

cards.heading: People to contact first
cards.text: Immediate family, physicians, attorneys, financial professionals, business partners, caregivers, veterinarians, and other people who may need to act quickly.

cards.heading: Important documents
cards.text: Insurance policies, property records, identification copies, legal documents, contracts, and directions to authoritative originals.

cards.heading: Accounts and digital access
cards.text: An inventory of important accounts, recovery contacts, password-manager instructions, backup methods, and explanations of what each account is used for.

cards.heading: Financial and cryptocurrency context
cards.text: Banking and investment information, Bitcoin or Ethereum wallet locations, exchange accounts, hardware-wallet notes, and carefully protected recovery instructions.

cards.heading: Household and dependent information
cards.text: Utilities, vehicles, alarm systems, medications, caregivers, school contacts, pet-care instructions, and urgent household details.

cards.heading: Personal instructions
cards.text: A short explanation of what should happen first, who should handle what, and any context that is difficult to reconstruct from documents alone.
